key_insight: Ω-QVLA demonstrates that a composite rotation transform combined with per-step scaling makes it possible to robustly quantize both the LLM backbone and the diffusion-based action (DiT) head to low-bit formats, removing the need for mixed-precision workarounds while preserving performance.
problem_solved: Large Vision-Language-Action models are too heavy for on-device use because prior quantization either left diffusion action heads at full precision or relied on mixed precision—quantizing DiT uniformly was considered unstable. Ω-QVLA solves stable, uniform low-bit quantization for the full VLA stack.
method: Composite rotation: apply structured rotations to weights/activations to decorrelate channels and concentrate representational energy into quantization-friendly bases.
Per-step scaling: introduce diffusion-step-specific scale factors to normalize dynamic ranges across generation steps, stabilizing quantization of the DiT action head.

Unified quantization pipeline: combine the above with calibration / light quantization-aware fine-tuning to enable uniform low-bit integer quantization for both backbone and action head with minimal accuracy loss.
impact: Enables substantial model-size and compute reductions for VLA systems so they can run on edge devices or cheaper cloud instances, simplifying deployment by eliminating mixed-precision complexity while keeping performance close to full precision.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: before vs after showing LLM + DiT head with mixed-precision baseline vs uniform quantized Ω-QVLA pipeline.
Mechanism schematic: small illustration of composite rotation (matrix rotate) + per-step scaling applied to diffusion steps.
Bar chart: model size / memory footprint and latency reductions at different bit-widths (e.g., FP16 vs 8-bit vs 4-bit) with corresponding performance drop.
Line plot: task metric (reward/accuracy) vs quantization bit-width demonstrating robustness across diffusion steps.
paper_title: Ω-QVLA: Robust Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models via Composite Rotation and Per-step Scaling
paper_authors: Xinyu Wang, Mingze Li, Sicheng Lyu, Dongxiu Liu, Kaicheng Yang
